es.title: Valores distintos con DISTINCT
es.summary: Quite las filas repetidas con DISTINCT y cuente valores diferentes con COUNT(DISTINCT …) en MySQL.
body: **`SELECT DISTINCT city`** devuelve cada ciudad una sola vez: hay ocho clientes, pero solo cinco ciudades, de `Bilbao` a `Valencia`.

`DISTINCT` se aplica a la fila entera, no a la primera columna. `SELECT DISTINCT category_id, active` da cinco combinaciones: las categorías `1`, `2` y `3` solo tienen productos activos (`1`), y la `4` aparece dos veces porque tiene uno inactivo (`0`, `Bananas 1 kg`) y otros activos.

Dentro de `COUNT`, **`COUNT(DISTINCT customer_id)`** cuenta valores diferentes: `10` pedidos, pero de solo `7` clientes, en `4` estados distintos y `4` meses (`MONTH(ordered)` saca el mes de la fecha; se verá con calma en la lección de fechas).
`active` sale como `1` y `0`: en MySQL, `BOOLEAN` es en realidad `TINYINT(1)`, un número pequeño, y `TRUE` y `FALSE` valen `1` y `0`.
points: Actúa sobre todas las columnas del `SELECT` a la vez.
es.exercise: Cuente cuántos productos distintos aparecen en `order_items` con `COUNT(DISTINCT product_id)`.

en.title: Distinct values with DISTINCT
en.summary: Remove repeated rows with DISTINCT and count different values with COUNT(DISTINCT …) in MySQL.
body: **`SELECT DISTINCT city`** returns each city once: there are eight customers but only five cities, from `Bilbao` to `Valencia`.

`DISTINCT` applies to the whole row, not to the first column. `SELECT DISTINCT category_id, active` gives five combinations: categories `1`, `2` and `3` only have active products (`1`), and `4` shows up twice because it has an inactive one (`0`, `Bananas 1 kg`) as well as active ones.

Inside `COUNT`, **`COUNT(DISTINCT customer_id)`** counts different values: `10` orders, but from only `7` customers, in `4` different statuses and `4` months (`MONTH(ordered)` takes the month out of the date; the dates lesson covers it properly).
`active` comes back as `1` and `0`: in MySQL, `BOOLEAN` is really `TINYINT(1)`, a small number, and `TRUE` and `FALSE` are `1` and `0`.
points: It works on all the columns of the `SELECT` at once.
en.exercise: Count how many different products appear in `order_items` with `COUNT(DISTINCT product_id)`.
